test a weighted combination using inverse_error weights, which may adapt to varying errors despite unstable ranking.
test a simple robust median combination to see if a more robust estimator improves over trimmed mean for this trend‑dominated, unstable ranking series.
test a softmax‑negative‑error weighted combination to see if a non‑linear weighting improves over trimmed mean on this trend‑dominated series.
test a weighted combination on the compact, low‑error pool (trend‑dominated series, unstable ranking) to see if inverse‑error weighting improves over trimmed mean.
The ranking is unstable and the series is trend-dominated; a robust DBA (dynamic Bayesian averaging) over the full pool may capture shifting model strengths better than static weighted combos.
ranking is unstable, so a per‑horizon best‑model weighting on the stable pool4 might capture horizon‑specific strengths.
test a per‑horizon top‑k mean on the compact pool4 to capture horizon‑specific strengths in this trend‑dominated, moderately seasonal series.
The series has unstable ranking and strong trend; try a per‑horizon best‑model weighting on a robust subset (pool5) to capture horizon‑specific strengths.
test a per‑horizon best‑model weighting on the full pool to capture horizon‑specific strengths in this trend‑dominated, non‑stationary series.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a robust median over a correlated‑error pool may improve stability.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8947. Series context: trend strength 0.7578 and seasonal strength 0.3586; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.107); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 2.325.
